inspection_outcome: Ten numbered findings: five Major issues in general torsion inputs/equivariant foundations/gerbe scope and five Minor local corrections.
summary: The unrestricted reading of the diagram-defined cover family in Proposition6.5 has an exact torsion counterexample; the actual coprime-degree motivic subclass is not identified here. Independently, its multi-factor reverse induction invokes a smooth-boundary lemma on a crossing boundary. Lemma6.18, the orbit site, coarse fixed stacks and arbitrary-gerbe scope have the separately recorded defects. Final Higgs-moduli conclusions are not disproved.

problems.title: Scope of the cover torsion claim and the singular-boundary induction
problems.source_location: Diagram(21) p23; definition/Proposition6.5 p25; Step2 p27
problems.claim: An unrestricted reading of Proposition6.5 for the diagram(21) family asserts torsion-freeness; the literal proposition does not separately quantify all l,k or specify the actual motivic parameter subclass.
problems.assumptions: C smooth projective genus2, Weierstrass c0,n2,l=(1,1),k=(1,1) define a positive-parameter finite etale cover. Membership in the actual coprime-degree motive is not established; Section6.2 has standing(d,n)=1.

problems.decisive_evidence: Y={(x,y,L):2L=AJx+AJy} is connected etale degree16. Pi=pi1C,A=(Z/2)^4,K=kerPi->A,Gamma=kerPi²->A. Hyperelliptic involution yields actual section and Gamma=K semidirect Pi. H2Pi=Z -> H2A=(Z/2)^6 has image span(a1 wedge b1+a2 wedge b2), order2. Hence H1K_A=Z4+(Z/2)^5, H1Y=Z8+(Z/2)^5, TorH²Y=(Z/2)^5. Step2 boundary is a crossing union locally xy0, violating Lemma6.7 smoothness.
problems.result: Unrestricted family reading is false. Independently, the multi-factor reverse induction invokes Lemma6.7 without its smooth closed-boundary hypothesis.
problems.impact: Core proof gap in the displayed induction used for the Higgs torsion reduction; not a verified counterexample to the actual motivic subclass or Theorem6.3.

problems.counterevidence: Prop6.5 does not explicitly say for all l,k. The preceding coprime-degree motivic construction may select a narrower subclass. The explicit example has sum(k_i*l_i)=2, not coprime to n2; its occurrence in that subclass is unproved. Repeated weights are not prohibited by the diagram or bundle calculation, but this does not prove membership. Coprimality does not remove the independent local crossing geometry of the Step2 product-open boundary.
problems.severity_basis: Major rests on the unmet smoothness hypothesis in an actual core induction, together with the explicitly limited failure of the unrestricted reading; not on an asserted false final theorem.

independent_acceptance_check.status: Scope corrected; independent core proof gap retained
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: For a genus2 curve with Weierstrass c0, hyperelliptic tau satisfies AJ(tau x)=-AJ(x). The positive diagram parameters n2,l=(1,1),k=(1,1) define connected degree16 finite-etale Y={(x,y,L):2L=AJx+AJy}. With Pi=pi1C,A=(Z/2)^4,K=ker(Pi->A), Gamma=ker(Pi^2->A) splits as K semidirect Pi through the actual section x->(x,tau x,O). The conjugation coinvariants are H1(K)_A. In the five-term sequence H2Pi=Z->H2A=(Z/2)^6, the surface class maps to the nonzero symplectic element a1 wedge b1+a2 wedge b2, of order2. Its cokernel is (Z/2)^5; the remaining free quotient 2Z^4 splits. Thus H1Y=Z^8 plus (Z/2)^5 and integral UCT gives TorH2(Y)=(Z/2)^5.
independent_acceptance_check.quantifier_and_assumption_limit: The literal Proposition6.5 does not explicitly quantify all l,k or list the motivic parameter subclass. Section6.2 assumes(d,n)=1. This example has sum(k_i l_i)=2, not coprime to n2, and is not verified to occur in the actual motivic expansion. Repeated weights are not forbidden by the diagram/bundle calculation, but that does not establish membership. The numerical counterexample is explicitly conditional on the unrestricted reading.
independent_acceptance_check.independent_core_gap: Step2 p.27 defines the product U=product_i(C^(l_i+1) minus C^(l_i)). Its complement is a union of coordinate divisors. Near their crossing the boundary union is t1*t2=0; the intersection itself is t1=t2=0. Finite-etale pullback preserves the crossing, so the closed boundary is not smooth as required by Lemma6.7. Coprimality does not change this local geometry. Reading U instead as the complement of the lower product does not preserve the stated product-open formula and affine calculation(25).
independent_acceptance_check.dependency_and_severity: The displayed multi-factor reverse induction is an actual step of the torsion reduction used for Theorem6.3; Major is based on its unmet hypothesis, not on an unproved final-theorem counterexample.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: The single-factor case and large-degree bundle mechanism do not supply this missing multi-factor induction. State the exact motivic parameter restrictions and prove a suitable torsion argument for them, or replace the reduction. No extra gcd condition alone is certified sufficient. Final coprime-degree Higgs-moduli torsion is not disproved.

independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: Take C1=Z{u,v},C0=Z{a,b},du=p b,dv=0. Define N0a=b,N1u=v, other values0. The local system on S1 becomes trivial on its degree-p cover and its fiber has pi0=Z plus Z/p,pi1=Z. In ConeN the degree1 images are a_s->b_t,u_t->p b_t, and degree2 u_s->-p b_s+v_t. problems.decisive_evidence: P|s(G)=empty yields allowed morphism P->E. Empty family covers E, its pullback is empty sieve on nonempty P, disallowed by A.6 image-union criterion. For free X=G, forcing generated topology makes every object empty-covered and sheaf category terminal, contradicting A.10 Sh(G;G)=Space.

problems.counterevidence: Counterexample is finite-dimensional locally compact Hausdorff complex analytic with nonempty fixed locus. Taking generated topology is not a repair. Does not itself refute final KU equivalence.

independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: For C2 acting on C by z->-z, let P=C* times(e\G) and E=empty times(G\G). The prescribed partial domain P|sG is empty, so the rule admits P->E. The empty family covers E; its pullback is the empty family over nonempty P, contrary to the stated image-union criterion. Empty objects and the partial-domain convention are explicitly allowed. If one instead generates a topology from the rule, for the free action X=G each generalized orbit maps to such an empty orbit; all objects acquire empty covers and the sheaf category becomes terminal, contrary to the asserted Sh_G(G)=Spaces.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_scope: This is a failure of the proposed general site and a foundation used by Section5. It is not a counterexample to the final K-theory equivalence.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Specify compatible morphisms and covering rules, then justify the needed orbit comparison, stalk, functoriality and base-change assertions. Deleting an isolated empty-object clause is not a certified replacement proof.

independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: Let the strict C2 action on BC3 invert C3. The coarse space is a point, so the coarse-fixed definition gives X^G=X. With H=G and U=X, the two representatives of the single coset H\G give identity and inversion functors. A natural isomorphism would require k r=r^{-1}k for generator r of the abelian group C3, which would force r=r^{-1}, impossible. Thus the action map does not descend independently of representatives even up to natural isomorphism.

problems.decisive_evidence: For alpha0, L_gamma'=O and group algebra gives C_c^0=M^gamma×c*, two components. Etale connected double curve cover has connected T*Pic1; deck involution is free since invariant odddegree line bundle would descend and have even degree. M^gamma quotient connected; Mtilde_gamma connected. Hence claimed torsor isomorphism impossible for alpha0.
problems.result: Cor6.16 cannot serve the stated arbitrary-Brauer scope without more input.
problems.impact: Cor6.16 cannot serve the stated arbitrary-Brauer scope without more input.

correction.statement: Explicitly restrict canonical-gerbe claim and separately prove any arbitrary-Brauer extension.

problems.counterevidence: If Cor6.16 intended only canonical gerbe, alpha0 example does not refute that restricted version. Theorem6.11 itself not disproved.

independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: Choose the zero Brauer class on the quotient stack with its neutral equivariant gerbe, so every character line L_gamma is trivial and multiplication is the ordinary group algebra. Thus for c=<gamma> the character cover is M^gamma times c*. For n2,d1,g_C>=2 and nonzero gamma in J[2], the corresponding connected etale double curve has rank1 Higgs moduli T*Pic^1, which is connected. Etale pushforward preserves degree by Euler characteristics. A deck-invariant odd-degree line bundle would admit a cyclic linearization over C and descend, forcing even degree; hence the deck action is free. Its quotient M^gamma is connected. The character cover for alpha0 has two components, while the geometric rank1 cover is connected.
independent_acceptance_check.assumption_test: The source distinguishes plain M from fixed-determinant Mcheck; Proposition6.15 here uses plain rank1 M, with no Norm/determinant constraint. The example uses the allowed coprime n2,d1 and the zero class on the quotient, not merely an underlying nonequivariantly trivial class.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_scope: If Corollary6.16 is read as only canonical-obstruction-gerbe specific, that restricted assertion is not refuted. It then cannot justify Theorem6.11's arbitrary-alpha argument without additional proof. No false final Theorem6.11 conclusion is claimed.
independent_acceptance_check.dependency_and_repair: The proof uses the universal-family obstruction property in the actual arbitrary-gerbe reduction. Track and retain the canonical-gerbe hypothesis, and prove any required extension to arbitrary Brauer classes separately.
